strengths: The paper addresses a timely problem: context-dependent watermarks are difficult to apply when diffusion language models generate tokens in arbitrary order. Combining an expectation over uncertain contexts with a predictive bias is a meaningful methodological contribution.

The empirical detection gains are substantial. Table 1 reports approximately 99% TPR at a nominal 1% FPR on both LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, compared with 49–83% for the naive adaptation at comparable measured quality.

The evaluation includes useful breadth: comparisons with Unigram, PatternMark, AAR, and KTH; an infilling experiment; and ablations of hashing, temperature, diffusion steps, remasking, context, and both proposed components.

Reusing a standard detector simplifies adoption. The appendices provide substantial experimental detail, runtime measurements, and an explanation of binomial testing with independent green-list entries.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.1 is false as stated. Appendix I assumes that every KL constraint is active and divides by its multiplier without establishing that the multiplier is positive. Constant coordinate objectives or sufficiently large KL budgets invalidate the claimed universal existence and uniqueness of a finite tilt satisfying KL = ε. Moreover, the coupled objective is generally nonconcave, so the fixed-point equation does not certify global optimality. These are substantive gaps in the claimed theoretical foundation.

Algorithm 1 does not implement the fixed-point map described in Section 3.2: it multiplies the previous iterate by the exponential tilt, whereas the stated map tilts the original model distribution. These coincide for one iteration but differ thereafter, undermining the interpretation of the multi-iteration ablation and any associated guarantee relative to the original distribution. Equation (8) also reverses the survival-function difference: the MinHash probability should be A(s) − A(s+1), not its negative.

The claim of negligible quality degradation is stronger than the evidence. For the recommended single-token context, log perplexity rises from 1.56 to 1.90 on LLaDA and from 1.94 to 2.32 on Dream, corresponding to roughly 40% and 46% increases in perplexity. GPT-4o scores fall from 8.95 to 8.43 and 8.45 to 7.76. Aggregate judge scores and perplexity do not establish preservation of factual accuracy or task performance.

The efficiency claim is overstated. Figure 17 reports generation times increasing from 8.94 seconds without watermarking to 11.52 and 15.08 seconds, approximately 29% and 69% overhead. Calling this minimal is difficult to justify, particularly when diffusion-model efficiency motivates the work.

Robustness and security conclusions exceed the experiments. Figure 3 shows paraphrasing detection remaining around 55–60% even for 200–400 tokens. There is no matched attack comparison establishing similar robustness to autoregressive watermarks; sharing a detector alone does not establish this. The assertion that larger contexts provide security against scrubbing or spoofing is also unsupported by direct attacks or a proof for the proposed hashes.

Statistical validation and sampling details leave practical uncertainty. The binomial argument establishes calibration over independent random green-list entries, but the paper lacks a substantial human-text evaluation across fixed keys and domains. Rejection sampling removes short and highly repetitive responses without reporting rejection rates by method, making quality and deployment-cost comparisons conditional on an incompletely characterized filter.

GPT-4o scores fall from 8.95 to 8.43 and from 8.45 to 7.76. These changes warrant stronger task-level or human quality evaluation and uncertainty estimates.

The efficiency characterization conflicts with the measurements. Figure 17 reports generation time increasing from 8.94 seconds to 11.52 or 15.08 seconds, approximately 29% or 69% overhead. Robustness and security claims exceed the evidence. Figure 3 lacks matched baseline attack curves, so it does not substantiate comparative robustness to autoregressive watermarks. Appendix B's assertion that larger contexts secure the method against stealing or spoofing is not demonstrated for these hash constructions; sharing a detector does not establish equivalent security.

The evaluation leaves deployment reliability insufficiently established. Length and repetition rejection sampling condition the reported results on accepted outputs, without reporting rejection rates. The binomial argument supports calibration over independently sampled green-list entries, but large-scale empirical false-positive validation on human text and variability across watermark keys are missing. These gaps matter for the claimed reliable provenance detection.

strengths: Addresses a timely problem: context-dependent watermarking when diffusion models generate tokens in arbitrary order. Combining an expected watermark boost with a predictive context bias is a useful, interpretable contribution.
Strong reported detection results: Table 1 reaches approximately 99% TPR at a nominal 1% FPR across two models and several contexts, substantially outperforming naive autoregressive adaptations.

The evaluation is extensive, including order-agnostic baselines (Unigram and PatternMark), AAR/KTH adaptations, infilling, and ablations over sampling schedules, temperature, hashing, approximation size, and both proposed components.
Reusing an inexpensive detector is practically attractive. The independent Bernoulli green-list construction and pair deduplication also provide a clean basis for the binomial null distribution.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.1 is false as stated. Appendix I.1 assumes, rather than establishes, that every KL constraint is active and divides by multipliers that may be zero. A finite, unique tilt need not exist when the objective is constant or the KL budget exceeds that needed to reach an optimum. For example, a uniform binary reference distribution cannot attain KL greater than log(2), although the theorem places no corresponding restriction on epsilon. Moreover, the coupled objective is generally nonconcave, so the stationarity equations do not certify global optimality. These issues undermine the claimed theoretical foundation.

The practical algorithm does not implement the stated fixed-point map beyond its first iteration. Section 3.2 defines the update using the original distribution p, whereas Algorithm 1, line 7, repeatedly tilts the current iterate. This accumulates distortions and need not preserve the original KL budget. Consequently, the multi-iteration experiments do not clearly validate the proposed solver. Equation (8) also reverses the MinHash probability difference: with the stated survival function, it should be A_t(s) minus A_t(s+1).

Claims of negligible quality degradation are stronger than the evidence. For the single-token context, Table 1 increases LLADA log-perplexity from 1.56 to 1.90 and reduces its judge score from 8.95 to 8.43; DREAM drops from 8.45 to 7.76. These are meaningful changes. Averaging style, consistency, accuracy, and ethics scores can obscure losses in factual accuracy, and there is no task-accuracy or human evaluation establishing preservation of utility.

The reported detection results are conditional on rejection sampling that excludes short and highly repetitive responses. Rejection rates and their variation across methods are not reported, leaving deployment-level detection, quality, and generation costs unclear. The paper also lacks a substantial human-text false-positive evaluation and clearly reported variability across watermark keys.

Robustness and security claims are insufficiently substantiated. Figure 3 lacks matched baseline attack curves, so using the same detector does not establish comparable robustness or an advantage from expectation-based watermarking. Paraphrasing leaves detection near 50–55% even for longer sequences. The assertion that larger contexts provide security against scrubbing and spoofing is not supported by attacks on the proposed construction.

The description of runtime overhead as minimal conflicts with Figure 17: generation rises from 8.94 seconds to 11.52 or 15.08 seconds, approximately 29% or 69% overhead. Suggested implementation optimizations are not demonstrated. Despite promising empirical results, the theoretical errors, algorithmic inconsistencies, and overstated practical claims require substantive revision before acceptance.

strengths: Addresses an important limitation of context-dependent watermarking in diffusion language models. Combining expected green-token boosting with predictive context bias is a meaningful, interpretable contribution.

Strong empirical detection results: approximately 99% TPR at a nominal 1% FPR across two models and several contexts, substantially outperforming naive autoregressive adaptations at comparable perplexity.
The evaluation is broad, including order-agnostic baselines, additional watermark families, infilling, decoding variations, component ablations, downstream benchmarks, and runtime measurements.
Reusing a lightweight detector is practically attractive. The 100-key, 10,000-text false-positive experiment provides useful evidence beyond detection accuracy alone.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.1 is false as stated. Appendix J.1 assumes active KL constraints and divides by their multipliers without establishing positivity. Inactive constraints, constant gradients, and boundary optima invalidate the claimed universal finite, unique exponential-tilt parameter. For example, maximizing a binary green-token indicator from p=(0.5,0.5) with epsilon greater than log(2) yields a deterministic optimum unattainable with finite delta. Moreover, the nonconcave objective means the fixed-point equation does not certify global optimality. The theorem and associated optimality claims need substantial qualification.

The claims of negligible quality degradation overstate the evidence. Table 3 shows LLADA MMLU decreasing from 65.01 to 55.13 with the recommended single-token context, and MBPP decreasing from 23.80 to 15.80 with the bidirectional context. DREAM GSM8K falls from 38.06 to 23.65 in that setting. Detection is primarily evaluated at temperature 0.5, whereas benchmark utility uses 0.1, so their joint detectability–utility trade-off remains unclear.

Security and robustness claims exceed the demonstrated results. Figure 3 shows paraphrasing detection remaining around 50–55% even at 400 tokens, and does not directly compare attacked baselines at matched quality and initial detectability. Assertions that larger contexts prevent spoofing or scrubbing are not supported by adaptive attack experiments for the proposed hashes.

False-positive guarantees need a clearer distinction between randomness over keys and performance with a deployed fixed key. The independent-entry binomial argument does not establish distribution-independent calibration for each fixed key; Table 2 itself reports a maximum 1.7% FPR at the nominal 1% threshold. The empirical improvement over Unigram is valuable, but categorical claims that this limitation does not apply are too strong.

Several technical presentation errors hinder verification. Equation (8) reverses the MinHash probability difference: the defined decreasing survival function requires A(s)-A(s+1). Algorithm 2 accepts an iteration count without implementing the iteration and overwrites q rather than explicitly assembling its position-wise distributions. These should be corrected and reconciled with the implementation.

strengths: Addresses a timely problem with a meaningful technical idea: combining an expected watermark boost with a predictive bias accommodates unknown context tokens during diffusion generation while retaining an inexpensive detector.
Reports substantial detection gains on two DLMs. Table 1 shows approximately 99% TPR at nominal 1% FPR, compared with 49–83% for the naive autoregressive adaptation at broadly comparable perplexity.

Evaluation is extensive: it includes order-agnostic baselines, additional watermark adaptations, infilling, downstream benchmarks, and ablations of both proposed components, hashing, temperature, diffusion steps, and approximation parameters.

The false-positive experiments across 100 keys and 10,000 unwatermarked samples provide useful empirical calibration evidence. Implementation details and an optimized runtime evaluation further support practical relevance.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.1 is false as stated. Appendix J assumes that every KL constraint is active and divides by its multiplier without establishing that the multiplier is positive. Constraints can be inactive, and an optimum on the simplex boundary may require an infinite exponential tilt. For example, with uniform p and epsilon greater than log vocabulary size, the asserted KL equality is impossible. Moreover, the nonconcave objective means the fixed-point equation does not certify global optimality. The acknowledged absence of convergence guarantees does not resolve these issues with the theorem itself.

The claim of minimal or negligible quality degradation overstates the results. In Table 3, LLADA MMLU falls from 65.01 to 55.13 with the recommended single-token context, and to 52.57 with the bidirectional context. DREAM GSM8K falls from 38.06 to 23.65 with the bidirectional context. Table 4 also shows substantial losses under entropy remasking. These are material utility costs, despite the more favorable DREAM single-context results.

Robustness claims exceed the comparative evidence. Figure 3 contains no matched baseline demonstrating similar robustness to autoregressive watermarks or superior context-aware substitution robustness. Paraphrasing leaves detection around 60–65% even at 300–400 tokens. Sharing a detector does not establish equal robustness because the generated watermark signal can differ.

Security and false-positive guarantees need narrower statements. Appendix B supports improved empirical calibration on one corpus, but random-key validity does not establish distribution-independent calibration for every deployed fixed key. Likewise, resistance to spoofing and scrubbing at larger context sizes is asserted without direct evaluation of the proposed hash implementations.

Several mathematical and algorithmic inconsistencies undermine reproducibility. Equation (8) reverses the MinHash probability difference: the defined survival function requires A(s) minus A(s+1), whereas the printed expression produces nonpositive probabilities. Algorithm 2 accepts an iteration count but never iterates over it and overwrites q instead of explicitly assembling its position-wise components.

The evaluation filters short and highly repetitive generations through rejection sampling without reporting rejection rates, leaving unconditional performance and generation cost unclear. Main results use 300 diffusion steps for 300 tokens; reduced-step experiments report detection curves without corresponding quality and runtime trade-offs. This limits the evidence for practical deployment in the accelerated generation regime motivating DLMs.

strengths: Addresses a timely, meaningful problem: context-dependent watermarking when diffusion language models generate tokens in arbitrary order. The combination of expectation boosting and predictive bias is intuitive and technically interesting.

Strong empirical detection improvements: Table 1 reports approximately 99% TPR at a nominal 1% FPR across two models and three context configurations, substantially outperforming the naive autoregressive adaptation.

Evaluation is extensive, including order-agnostic baselines, additional watermark families, infilling, task accuracy, attacks, runtime measurements, and ablations of both proposed components, sampling strategies, and approximation parameters.
Reuses an inexpensive detector and provides detailed experimental settings. The empirical false-positive study across 100 keys and 10,000 unwatermarked samples is particularly useful.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.1 is false without additional assumptions. Appendix J assumes active KL constraints and divides by their multipliers without establishing positivity. For example, maximizing a binary green indicator with p=(1/2,1/2) and epsilon>log(2) yields a deterministic optimum with an inactive constraint, which no finite exponential tilt represents. Constant gradients also invalidate uniqueness. Moreover, the nonconcave objective means fixed-point solutions need not be globally optimal; the practical update should be presented as a heuristic unless stronger conditions are established.

The repeated claim of negligible quality degradation overstates the results. Table 3 shows LLADA MMLU declining from 65.01 to 55.13 with the recommended single-token context, and DREAM GSM8K declining from 38.06 to 23.65 with the bidirectional context. Table 1 also shows appreciable perplexity and judge-score deterioration. Detection is primarily measured at temperature 0.5, while task accuracy uses 0.1, leaving the joint utility–detectability trade-off on those tasks unresolved.

Security claims exceed the evidence. Appendix B asserts security against spoofing and scrubbing at larger context sizes without testing these attacks or proving security for the proposed hash constructions. SumHash and MinHash compress many contexts into shared hashes, so increasing context size alone does not establish resistance. Likewise, sharing an autoregressive detector does not establish equivalent robustness of the resulting generation scheme.

False-positive guarantees require more careful qualification. The binomial argument averages over random green matrices; it does not guarantee nominal error for every fixed deployed key and arbitrary text distribution. The paper recognizes this distinction for Unigram but overstates its own exemption: Table 2 still reports a maximum 1.7% FPR at a nominal 1% threshold for the recommended single-token context.

Robustness to stronger edits remains limited: Figure 3 shows paraphrasing detection around 55–60% even for roughly 300–400 tokens. There is no matched autoregressive comparison supporting the claimed robustness advantage for context-aware substitutions. Rejection sampling of short or repetitive responses also conditions the headline evaluation on accepted outputs, without reporting rejection rates.

Several mathematical and algorithmic details need correction for reproducibility. Equation (8) reverses the MinHash probability difference: with the stated survival function, it should be A_t(s)-A_t(s+1). Algorithm 2 omits the advertised fixed-point iteration and overwrites q rather than explicitly updating q_t. These issues compound the uncertainty around the theoretical derivation.
